result.strongest_objection: The claimed success metric—100% of pi role directives contain the contract elements—is not established by the proposed tests. Arm 2 constructs synthetic directives inside the test rather than exercising the controller's actual directive-composition path. It can pass while every real directive omits the contract. This conflicts with the document's explicit deferral of linting real compositions and makes the central acceptance claim unsupported.
result.catch: Distinguish recipe-text conformance and checker-fixture coverage from actual directive conformance. The negative control proves only that the test-local checker rejects its chosen counter-example; it does not prove that controllers incorporate the new recipe block.
result.proposed_fix: Replace the 100% success metric with: "The shared pi recipe contains the required artifact-contract guidance; string assertions pin its normative clauses, and synthetic positive/negative fixtures test the local checker's recognition of those clauses. These tests do not measure or guarantee conformance of actual controller-composed directives. Real-composition linting remains deferred." Rename Arm 2 to "synthetic directive checker fixtures" and remove claims that this suite verifies prevention or compliance of real directives. If retaining the 100% metric, identify and verify an existing production composition entry point and test directives produced through that entry point rather than a test-local reconstruction.

result.strongest_objection: The primary success metric ('100 % of pi role directives composed under the recipe contain the four contract elements — checked by generated-directive arms in the new test suite, not by hoping') is vacuous: Arm 2 of the test suite only generates a hardcoded synthetic directive inside $SCRATCH and checks that synthetic string against itself. Because directives are composed dynamically by the LLM controller at runtime and no pre-spawn linter is wired into `scripts/mission_pi_run.sh` (explicitly deferred in Future Work), the test suite provides zero verification of actual directives composed in production, relying entirely on 'hoping' the controller LLM obeys the prose.
result.catch: In Goals -> Success Metrics and Testing Strategy -> Arm 2, the doc claims the test suite verifies generated-directive conformance rather than 'hoping', when in reality Arm 2 is a tautological test where the bash script authors both the synthetic directive string and the regex that checks it.
result.proposed_fix: Either (1) wire the directive-conformance checker into `scripts/mission_pi_run.sh` (which is inside the fleet Authority allowlist per V21: `scripts/mission_*`) so it lints the actual `--directive-file` before spawning `pi` and fails fast on missing contract markers, OR (2) revise 'Goals -> Success Metrics' and 'Examples -> Example 1' to remove the false claim that composed directives are mechanically checked, stating honestly: '100% of recipe copies contain the contract block and marker pins (checked by `test_gate3_artifact_contract.sh`); actual controller directive composition remains unlinted prose guidance until Future Work item 3 lands.'

result.strongest_objection: The primary Success Metric — "100 % of pi role directives composed under the recipe contain the four contract elements … checked by generated-directive arms in the new test suite, not by hoping" — is not instrumented by anything in this design and cannot be certified by its own acceptance run. Arm 2 checks only a synthetic directive the suite generates itself plus one counter-example; no mechanism anywhere in M1/M2 inspects a real controller-composed directive. The doc concedes this in Future Work ("this design lints the recipe text and synthetic directives only; linting real compositions is a controller-workflow change, attended"), so the Success Metrics section asserts a population-level prevention claim that the plan's own text admits is unmeasured. A done-gate built on this would certify an unmeasured claim, which is precisely the empty-but-successful-result shape the contract's own missing-input rule (and A11) forbids.
result.catch: Three load-bearing items to verify or fix before approval: (1) The new block is inserted immediately after PI_EVALUATOR_SESSION_HANDSHAKE_END (gate-3-route.md:522), yet the doc never records what the handshake block (lines 494–522, ~28 lines) currently prescribes about identity/session metadata — V18 only greps markers. If the handshake block already instructs evaluators on provider/model or session-state handling, the new identity-disposition norm could duplicate or contradict adjacent standing text, and Arms 1–4 would pin the conflict verbatim. (2) The Planner-Lane field asserts derive-planner-lane.sh "would emit opus fail-closed:path-not-in-codex-allowlist" from reading the script rather than running it (V23 is a read, not an execution), and the doc flags only gate-3-route.md as outside the mission-control.sh:1439 default when make/test.mk — a changed path — is outside that default too. (3) "No overlap in files" with m-fleet-slot-kill-reaps-descendants-sprint-plan.md is asserted, but if that sibling wires its suite via make/test.mk's LAUNCHD_SUITES (this doc's own wiring pattern), the two plans share a file and a merge-order surface that is nowhere addressed.
result.proposed_fix: Three concrete edits: (a) Replace the first Success Metrics bullet with: "Recipe-level pins hold: the contract block's four element names, the prohibition strings, the preserved rc18 retry wording, and the sanitized $HOME-literal example are present in both mirrors and pinned by the suite, and the suite's checker is shown to discriminate (flags the identity-research counter-example, passes the conformant synthetic). Conformance of real controller-composed directives is NOT measured by this design; a Gate-3 composition lint is Future Work (attended). The success claim is limited to: the standing instruction exists, is mirrored, and is regression-pinned." (b) Add Verification Log row V28: "read gate-3-route.md:494–522 (handshake block content) → record its current identity/session-metadata instructions → reconcile the identity-disposition wording with that block (or record non-overlap) before M1 drafting." (c) Add row V29: "run tools/launchd/derive-planner-lane.sh against this doc's Files section (read-only, bounded) → record the observed emission string" and amend the Planner-Lane paragraph to state that both .claude/skills/mission-control/resources/gate-3-route.md and make/test.mk fall outside the mission-control.sh:1439 default; add row V30 diffing the slot-kill sibling's changed paths against this doc's four paths, with a merge-order note if make/test.mk overlaps.
